findings.title: P8: options-dialog money fields and the grid-fee bound resolve the instance currency while every figure is the feed's
findings.claim: On a replayed install whose price feed declares HUF on a SEK-configured Home Assistant, 3 of 6 money surfaces resolve the instance currency (the options money-field label and its maximum, and the grid-fee rules bound), so a 20 HUF/kWh grid fee -- which the integration's own price_currency repair issue says must be entered in HUF -- is refused by both the field (max 5) and the rules validator (bound 10), while the entities, the repair issue and the coordinator's fee notice all resolve HUF.
findings.mechanism: currency.py's precedence (the feed's declared code first, the instance label only where the feed declares none) is applied by the coordinator (_feed_currency or resolve_currency) for entity units and the runtime fee notice, but config_flow._money, config_flow._fee_placeholders and OptionsFlow._grid_fee_errors call resolve_currency(hass) alone; money_scale/fee_bound therefore scale by the label, not by the currency the entered numbers are in.

evidence.unit: divergent surfaces of 6 (feed HUF, instance SEK)
evidence.machine: box B7, 4 vCPU Linux container, /root/venv-ci python
evidence.contention_note: two other finder seats on the box; counts are contention-immune

perturbation.change: --perturb: config_flow.resolve_currency resolves the price feed's declared code first (currency.declared_currency on the price entity's unit/attributes), as the coordinator does

findings.metric_definition: Of six money surfaces of one replayed install (feed HUF, instance SEK), how many resolve to SEK or refuse a 20 HUF/kWh fee the HUF bound admits.
findings.phenomenon_property: Every surface that labels, bounds or validates a money amount resolves its currency by the same precedence as the published figures (the feed's declared code, then the instance label); no surface asks the user for an amount in one currency and bounds it in another.
findings.seam_rule: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D14/s3/p8_surfaces.py  (prints each surface and its resolved currency; grep -n 'resolve_currency(' custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/*.py lists the call sites that skip the feed)

null_control.note: feed and instance both HUF: every surface agrees, field max 250, rules bound 500, 20 HUF/kWh accepted. Pre-fix re-find at 3490cb16 (git archive): 5 divergent (null arm 3, the bounds then unscaled).

reproduction_steps: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D14/s3/p8_surfaces.py   -> huf_feed_sek_instance_divergent_surfaces=3 (S3 'SEK/kWh', S4 'refuses 20: above the maximum 5', S5 error grid_fee_rules_implausible, bound '10'); huf_instance 0
findings.proposed_fix_scope: One resolver for a money amount's currency that takes the feed first (currency.py), called by config_flow._money, _fee_placeholders and _grid_fee_errors as by the coordinator; the price_currency_mismatch text then stops contradicting the dialog. Barrier: p8_surfaces' arms as a tests/replay.py control (counts, <10 s).

findings.title: N-reap-lock: an entry unload cancels its refresh but not the solve, so the reloaded entry's first solve waits out every orphan
findings.claim: When an entry is unloaded (an options save reloads it) while a solve is in flight, async_shutdown cancels the refresh task awaiting coordinator._await_process but the executor thread keeps running _run_in_process under _PROCESS_LOCK, and nothing on the unload path reaps the worker, so the new entry's first job waits out the orphan's remaining time (ratio 1.00) and, after three reloads, out three whole orphaned solves (17.0 s behind 6 s jobs, 2.83x one job).
findings.mechanism: Teardown ordered behind the lock a solve holds, on the unload seam: the stop path (_shutdown_process_pool, HA stop only) kills first and bounds its lock wait to 5 s (guarded, 0.00 s measured), but async_unload_entry -> async_shutdown only cancels the asyncio side; run_in_executor cannot cancel a started thread, and each orphan job still queued on _PROCESS_LOCK runs its full solve after acquiring it, its result discarded.

evidence.unit: s wall for a 0 s job submitted after 3 cancelled 6 s refreshes (reload3_first_job_wall_s); single reload 5.00 s = 1.00 x the orphan's remaining time
evidence.machine: box B7, 4 vCPU Linux container, /root/venv-ci python, real process_worker child
evidence.contention_note: provisional: two other finder seats on the box (load1 ~9); the jobs are time.sleep in the real worker, so the wall is set by the job length, not by CPU contention

perturbation.change: --reap-on-unload: after the cancel, the unload also runs coordinator._shutdown_process_pool on the executor (what HA's stop already does)
perturbation.observed_value: reload3 17.00 s -> 0.04 s; reload 5.00 s -> 0.03 s

findings.metric_definition: Wall seconds from submitting a 0 s job through coordinator._await_process to its return, after N refreshes awaiting 6 s jobs were cancelled as async_shutdown cancels them.
findings.phenomenon_property: No teardown of an entry (stop, unload, reload) leaves a solve it no longer wants holding _PROCESS_LOCK or the worker: the next entry's first solve never waits on an orphaned one, and orphaned solves never run.
findings.seam_rule: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D14/s3/reap_lock.py  (stop and reload seams); grep -n '_PROCESS_LOCK\|_shutdown_process_pool\|refresh.cancel' custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/*.py lists the lock's holders and the teardown paths

null_control.note: the same calls with no job in flight. The stop seam is guarded: stop_wall_s=0.00 s with a 6 s job in flight, and 5.00 s when the kill is made a no-op (--perturb), the _SHUTDOWN_LOCK_TIMEOUT_S bound.

reproduction_steps: ... --perturb -> stop_wall_s=5.00 (the stop seam's own guard moves)
findings.proposed_fix_scope: async_unload_entry (or async_shutdown) reaps the worker the way the stop path does when a refresh it cancelled had a job in the worker -- kill first, bounded swap -- so the orphan's read breaks and its queued siblings fail fast; or a per-job generation token checked after acquiring _PROCESS_LOCK so a job whose awaiter was cancelled is dropped before it runs. Real cost on a Raspberry Pi: solves of median 18 s, max 426 s (the constants' own comment), one discarded per options save during a solve.

findings.title: P10: the what-if's schedule pricing simulates reference days on the event loop; the replay barrier's DHW-only day never reaches it
findings.claim: Replaying the owner's recorded day (tests/replay/owner-2026-10-30-away.json, 1 h) through the real coordinator runs 384 ThermalModel.simulate_step calls on the event loop -- all via coordinator.async_simulate(steady=True) -> whatif.schedule_days -> HeatPumpOptimizer.reference_day -> _compute_baseline_power, reached from the fuse advisor's cycle step -- while tests/replay.py's P10 barrier, which replays only synthetic-dhw-only.json, reads 0 on the loop.
findings.mechanism: async_simulate prices a schedule ask inline: whatif.schedule_days calls reference_day on both the live and the what-if optimizer in the coordinator's own coroutine, and each distinct day is simulated twice over a day of steps; every other model kernel of the what-if goes through _await_optimize/_await_off_loop. The same call is reached by the what-if service (services.py, steady=True), the power-cap price tiles and the fuse advisor. The barrier's single fixture has no fuse/power-cap configuration, so its loop count is structurally 0.

evidence.unit: model-kernel calls on the event-loop route over 2 replayed cycles (owner-1h_loop); 773 over 4 cycles on the 2 h arm
evidence.machine: box B7, 4 vCPU Linux container, /root/venv-ci python
evidence.contention_note: counts are contention-immune; the loop CPU of those calls, 18.8 ms on this box at load1 10.9, is provisional

findings.instrumented_symbol: heatpump_optimizer.thermal_model:ThermalModel.simulate_step (counted by route via process_worker:run_worker and FakeHass.async_add_executor_job flags); site heatpump_optimizer.whatif:schedule_days / heatpump_optimizer.optimizer:HeatPumpOptimizer.reference_day

perturbation.change: P10_PERTURB_WHATIF=1: whatif.schedule_days returns None (no reference day priced)

findings.metric_definition: Model-kernel calls made in the coordinator's interpreter outside process_worker.run_worker and outside any executor job, over a replayed fixture, counted once at the outermost kernel.
findings.phenomenon_property: No model kernel (ThermalModel.simulate_*, the sysid fit, a reference-day or baseline simulation) runs on the event loop on any path a configured install reaches -- the cycle, its advisors, the what-if service and the price tiles -- on every replay fixture, not only the DHW-only one.

reproduction_steps: PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round11/D14/s3/p10_routes.py --arm owner-1h  -> owner-1h_loop=384, stack loop optimizer.py:_compute_baseline_power <- optimizer.py:reference_day <- whatif.py:schedule_days <- coordinator.py:async_simulate <- coordinator.py:_maybe_run_fuse_advisor
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Run whatif.schedule_days's two reference_day calls through _await_off_loop (both optimizers and inputs are already picklable job arguments of _await_optimize); and widen tests/replay.py's P10 arm to every committed fixture (or a fixture with the fuse advisor and power-cap tiles on), so the barrier enumerates the seams a full install reaches.
